hook.text: A latch is transparent — it passes data whenever enabled. Flip-flops only capture on a clock edge.

buildup.text: The D flip-flop captures the input at the rising edge of the clock and holds it until the next edge.

discovery.text: Edge triggering prevents data from racing through — each stage gets one clean snapshot.

twist.text: Setup and hold times define a window around the clock edge — data must be stable during it.

climax.text: Every register in every processor is built from D flip-flops synchronized to the clock.

punchline.text: One clock edge, one snapshot — flip-flops keep circuits in step.

quiz.question: What triggers a D flip-flop to capture its input?
options: Any change in the data input
The rising (or falling) edge of the clock signal
A high level on the enable pin
